angleRead.name: Elliot Graye
angleRead.text: Three congregations answered a crisis in the same cycle, C117, and I want to write about how they did it. Adams Point United Methodist activated an emergency assistance fund (attendance 50). Temple Beth Or held a vigil for community healing (91). Masjid An-Nur Oakland organized a community grief gathering (56). The ledger doesn't say what the crisis was, and I won't guess in print. First I'll find out whether the three rows answer one event or three separate ones. Then I'll go to the three leaders, Rev. Daniel Han, Rabbi Naomi Sterling and Imam Aziz Rahimi, and ask what happened, who came, what they asked for, and what the room did afterward. I'm after the quiet work: who made the calls, who

plan.focus: Three crisis responses in C117, at Adams Point United Methodist, Temple Beth Or and Masjid An-Nur Oakland, and the ordinary weekly work each congregation does behind them.
plan.why: Three crisis_response rows in one cycle across Methodist, Reform Jewish and Muslim congregations is the kind of quiet interfaith work that doesn't make headlines. The ledger gives what each did and how many came, but not why, so reporting is needed. I can't state the cause without the leaders.
checks: Do the three C117 rows answer one event or separate ones? The ledger doesn't say.
Masjid An-Nur is listed under East Oakland in the Faith_Ledger and Fruitvale in the candidate profile. Confirm where it is before printing a neighborhood.
What did the Adams Point emergency fund pay for, who could apply, and how much was disbursed? Get the figures from Han, not from the ledger.
Are the attendance figures (50, 91, 56) head counts from the congregations or ledger estimates?
Check the archive again for earlier Tribune coverage of these rows. My recall came back empty, which isn't proof there was none.

targets.question: Your congregation activated an emergency assistance fund this cycle. What happened that made you open it, who has come asking, and what has it been able to cover so far?
targets.basis: Leads Adams Point United Methodist, which activated the emergency assistance fund in C117 (attendance 50).

targets.question: Temple Beth Or held a vigil for community healing this cycle, and opened its doors for community support once before, in C104. Who was in the room, and what did you want them to leave with?
targets.basis: Leads Temple Beth Or, which held the C117 vigil (attendance 91).

targets.question: Masjid An-Nur organized a community grief gathering this cycle. Who asked for it, who came, and how does it sit alongside the lunches, pantry and tutoring the masjid already runs?
targets.basis: Leads Masjid An-Nur Oakland, which organized the C117 grief gathering (attendance 56).

plan.interpretation: Three different faiths each reached for a different tool in the same cycle: money, a vigil, a gathering for grief. That suggests a shared event or season of hardship, but I haven't established that. It may also be three unrelated things. Either way the story is how each community responded, not what set it off.
unverifiedLead: Whether the three C117 crisis rows respond to the same event.
Whether the congregations coordinated, perhaps through the Interfaith Council, which met in C114 and C115.
Whether the Adams Point fund has been drawn on, and by how many people.
